section_summary: This section records occupation-era changes to Japan’s foreign exchange system, including import controls, a yen counterpart fund for U.S. aid, and the adoption of a single rate of 360 yen per dollar. It also contains correspondence about private remittances and document confidentiality, press coverage of the new rate, and a Bolivian request for the return of funds blocked in Japan.

subfiles.title: Foreign Exchange Control Board, SCAPIN 1968
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The directive establishes a Foreign Exchange Control Board and defines its powers and working arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages assign the board control of foreign exchange transactions, access to Bank of Japan records and facilities, and reporting duties to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Request to discuss government papers with counsel
subfiles.about: Torson asks to discuss her government-related files with attorney W. R. Clements.
subfiles.summary: After moving to Clements’s office, Torson seeks permission to obtain his legal advice concerning files she has treated as confidential.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning classification of Torson’s papers
subfiles.about: Snight replies that he found no classified State Department documents supplied to Torson.
subfiles.summary: Snight says Kennedy is in Europe and that no classified document appears to have been made available to Torson.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department transmittal of Torson correspondence
subfiles.about: Swayze forwards material with the comment that it does not seem to concern the Office of International Trade.
subfiles.summary: Swayze notes that the matter does not appear to apply to his office.

subfiles.title: Request for permission to discuss banking and trade matters
subfiles.about: Torson seeks clearance to discuss her government-related banking and foreign trade work with Clements.
subfiles.summary: She describes earlier wartime work, her treatment of papers as confidential, and her concern that a presidential order may restrict discussion with her attorney.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government may be permitted to adopt liberalized import procedures
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch explains how SCAP’s new import-planning directive could expand Japanese control over imports.
subfiles.summary: It encloses SCAPIN 1982 and anticipates greater roles for the Foreign Exchange Control Board and private importers.

subfiles.title: Import Procedure, SCAPIN 1982
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP directs Japan to propose procedures for imports financed by export proceeds.
subfiles.summary: The requested plan must cover quarterly import programs, licenses, and criteria for approving specific imports.

subfiles.title: Press release on revised import procedures
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The airgram relays SCAP’s public explanation of the proposed import system.
subfiles.summary: It reports that Japan must plan imports purchased with export proceeds and that many imports may move to a private basis.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about remitting payment to a Japanese artist
subfiles.about: Piper asks how he can pay the Kyoto artist Insho for materials received.
subfiles.summary: Piper seeks a lawful way to send money to a Japanese citizen.

subfiles.title: Cosmic Art project outline
subfiles.about: Piper solicits examples of modern religious and metaphysical art for a book.
subfiles.summary: The circular lists desired artistic qualities, media, and chapter subjects for a planned book.

subfiles.title: Reply on remittances to Japan
subfiles.about: The State Department explains conditions for sending funds to Insho in Kyoto.
subfiles.summary: Rosenson suggests American banks with Japanese branches and explains that Insho would receive yen, possibly at 270 per dollar.

subfiles.title: Further explanation of Torson’s files
subfiles.about: Torson explains why she has treated her papers as confidential and wishes to consult Clements.
subfiles.summary: She recounts wartime assignments and later inquiries, questions the meaning of classification, and says she will discuss matters with Clements when needed.

subfiles.title: Correction to Torson’s previous letter
subfiles.about: Torson supplies a file reference omitted from her March 27 letter.
subfiles.summary: She adds the reference IR 894.5151 to her earlier correspondence.

subfiles.title: Exchange rate for the yen
subfiles.about: Fearey reports divided views on SCAP’s requested discretion to change the yen rate.
subfiles.summary: He forwards the National Advisory Council staff report and notes Army support for allowing SCAP a ten-percent adjustment without Washington review.

subfiles.title: Proposed single rate of exchange for Japanese yen and related measures
subfiles.about: The committee evaluates SCAP’s proposal for a unified yen exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: The draft examines a proposed 330-yen rate, import subsidies, inflation, export competitiveness, and an aid counterpart fund. It supports a single rate while warning that 330 may overvalue the yen and discussing a rate as high as 360.

subfiles.title: Alternative exchange-rate recommendations
subfiles.about: The notes compare alternative wording for National Advisory Council advice on the initial yen rate.
subfiles.summary: Both alternatives allow 330 to 360 yen per dollar and address later rate changes.

subfiles.title: Exchange rate for the yen: Army communications
subfiles.about: The memorandum reviews competing cables and the procedure for authorizing Japan’s new rate.
subfiles.summary: It discusses Army and State wording, MacArthur’s authority, and advance notice to the International Monetary Fund.

subfiles.title: Draft interim directive on a single yen rate
subfiles.about: The draft authorizes a unified yen rate and recommends consideration of 360 per dollar.
subfiles.summary: It sets a 330-yen authorized rate, urges consideration of 360, and refers later changes to Washington.

subfiles.title: Voorhees cable to Dodge on Council action
subfiles.about: Voorhees conveys the National Advisory Council’s exchange-rate resolution to Dodge.
subfiles.summary: The Council accepts 330 yen per dollar but strongly recommends considering a rate up to 360. Subsequent changes require Council consideration.

subfiles.title: Draft formal authorization for SCAP
subfiles.about: The draft treats the Council’s resolution as formal authorization to establish the yen rate.
subfiles.summary: It also records State’s strong support for considering the higher rate.

subfiles.title: SCAP accepts recommended yen rate
subfiles.about: SCAP accepts the Washington-recommended rate and anticipates announcement after Diet budget action.
subfiles.summary: The message says the rate will be released after passage of Japan’s budget bill.

subfiles.title: Establishment of U.S. Aid Counterpart Fund for Japanese Stabilization
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch describes Japan’s planned yen fund corresponding to U.S. aid shipments.
subfiles.summary: It explains SCAPIN 1988, the proposed ¥175 billion budget entry, and debate over the fund’s management and legal basis. The allocation suggestions reported by the Japanese press remained speculative.

subfiles.title: Yen counterpart of GARIOA and EROA imports, SCAPIN 1988
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP orders a yen account matching the dollar cost of U.S. aid to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Deposits must reflect aid costs at a SCAP-specified rate. Withdrawals require SCAP approval and consideration of stabilization, debt retirement, credit, and investment goals.

subfiles.title: Government ordered to set up aid counterpart fund
subfiles.about: The article reports SCAP’s order establishing the U.S. aid counterpart fund.
subfiles.summary: It describes deposits, SCAP-controlled withdrawals, and potential uses for debt retirement and stabilization.

subfiles.title: Present status of yen counterpart fund
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports unresolved administrative details delaying the aid counterpart fund.
subfiles.summary: An ESS meeting identified slow documentation of U.S. aid shipments, uncertainties over valuation, and questions about Japanese agency control. Marquat assigned Sherwood M. Fine to resolve technical issues; implementation was expected to take several weeks.

subfiles.title: Confidential advance release to Australian ambassador
subfiles.about: State forwards an embargoed SCAP press release.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador is asked to keep the release confidential until its announced Washington release time.

subfiles.title: Confidential advance release to British ambassador
subfiles.about: State forwards an embargoed SCAP press release.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador is asked to keep the release confidential until its announced Washington release time.

subfiles.title: Establishment of single exchange rate and summary of press comment
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports adoption of a 360-yen dollar rate and surveys reactions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The new rate took effect April 25, 1949, and applied to permitted foreign exchange and aid-counterpart transactions. Japanese officials and business groups generally welcomed it while debating effects on exports, prices, subsidies, and the budget. The despatch encloses the directive, press release, and related articles.

subfiles.title: Establishment of official exchange rate for Japanese yen, SCAPIN 1997
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP directs Japan to implement a 360-yen dollar rate on April 25.
subfiles.summary: The directive applies the rate to permitted trade, exchange, and counterpart-fund deposits, while specifying how existing export contracts and imported input costs must be handled.

subfiles.title: Announce yen rate
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, Far East Command
subfiles.about: SCAP publicly announces the 360-yen rate and its application.
subfiles.summary: The release explains treatment of trade transactions and existing contracts, linking the rate to stabilization while noting that currency conversion restrictions remain.

subfiles.title: New single rate held favorable to export trade
subfiles.about: The article collects Japanese official, political, and business reactions to the new rate.
subfiles.summary: Most respondents welcome the rate while urging industrial efficiency and selective price adjustments.

subfiles.title: 80% of goal fixed for export trade may be attained
subfiles.about: The article presents Economic Stabilization Board estimates for exports and tourism at the new rate.
subfiles.summary: It forecasts attainment of roughly 80 percent of the export goal and identifies industries likely to fall short.

subfiles.title: Budget’s revision said unnecessary
subfiles.about: The article reports Cabinet decisions on the budget and prices after the new rate.
subfiles.summary: Officials see no immediate budget revision, though some prices and import subsidies may require adjustment.

subfiles.title: Fears are groundless, Dodge Mission asserts
subfiles.about: Dodge Mission members answer concerns that the new exchange rate will burden the counterpart fund.
subfiles.summary: They explain that the estimated fund amount is provisional and deposits derive from sales of U.S. aid goods.

subfiles.title: Bolivian request for return of blocked Japanese credit
subfiles.about: Bolivia requests release of a credit held by a Tokyo firm for Gumucio y Compañía.
subfiles.summary: The embassy asserts that the Bolivian firm legally acquired the $25,351.38 claim and asks U.S. authorities to arrange its return.

subfiles.title: Commercial registry certificate for Gumucio y Compañía
subfiles.from: National Registrar of Commerce, La Paz
subfiles.about: The certificate records Gumucio’s acquisition of Kyllmann, Bauer’s assets and liabilities.
subfiles.summary: It states that overseas funds listed in the acquired firm’s balance sheet belong to Gumucio.

subfiles.title: Bolivian legal opinion on blocked credit
subfiles.about: A Bolivian legal officer supports Gumucio’s claim to funds blocked in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The report traces the credit to prewar Bolivian exports, describes Gumucio’s acquisition of the original firm’s assets, and recommends seeking its return.

subfiles.title: English translation of Bolivian diplomatic note
subfiles.from: Embassy of Bolivia; translated by Department of State
subfiles.about: The translation repeats Bolivia’s request for the Tokyo credit’s return.
subfiles.summary: It identifies the claimed $25,351.38 and the documents offered to establish Gumucio’s ownership.

subfiles.title: English translation of commercial registry certificate and authentications
subfiles.from: National Registrar of Commerce, La Paz; translated by Department of State
subfiles.about: The translated certificate and endorsements establish Gumucio’s ownership of acquired overseas assets.
subfiles.summary: It reproduces the registry finding and subsequent authentications of the registrar’s signature and seal.

subfiles.title: English translation of Bolivian legal opinion
subfiles.from: Emilio Díaz Romero; translated by Department of State
subfiles.about: The translated legal report recounts Gumucio’s claim to a blocked Tokyo credit.
subfiles.summary: This opening page traces the credit to prewar Bolivian exports and explains why it remained blocked.
